h: Bog bodies, planes and a Cheshire day out
p: Wilmslow might feel like a quiet commuter town, but it has a few surprises up its sleeve. The Lindow Moss peat bog on the edge of town is where Lindow Man was discovered in 1984, an incredibly well-preserved Iron Age body that's now on display in the British Museum. Kids tend to find that story deliciously gruesome, and it's a fun fact to throw at them on the drive over.

For the session itself, a weekday after-school slot or an early weekend booking can be a calmer bet than peak Saturday afternoon. Give yourselves time to get changed and sorted, and keep a bag in the car with a change of clothes and some water for afterwards. Teens will happily do a whole session flat out; little ones might want a sit-down halfway, and that's fine.

Plane-mad kids are well placed here, because Manchester Airport is just up the road. The Runway Visitor Park beside the airfield has close-up views of take-offs and landings and, as a bonus, a real Concorde to look at. If you'd rather head the other way, Alderley Edge has National Trust woodland walks along a sandstone ridge with big views across the Cheshire Plain. The National Trust's Quarry Bank at Styal, with its working cotton mill and gardens, is another easy add-on for a gentler afternoon. Wilmslow station has trains to Manchester and beyond, so it's reachable without a car as well.
